A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REN research work. All 15 pages of each version, including Appendices A–C, equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original REN runtime, segmentation and retrieval results, plus ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original REN experiments and appendix analyses, including benchmark results and comparisons of training objectives.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix A replace SAM 2 with SAM as the reported source of masks defining contrastive positives and pooled feature targets. This revises a training supervision component; REN's architecture, loss formulas and inference procedures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether training was rerun or the description was corrected.

E1.justification: Both versions use Ego4D for training and visual query localization, ADE20K and VOC2012 for segmentation, and COCO-based Visual Haystacks and image retrieval evaluations. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the runtime, VQ2D, segmentation, Visual Haystacks and image retrieval comparisons. SAM 2 remains a runtime comparator despite the revised training-mask description.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the specified preprocessing tool from the SAM 2 Automatic Mask Generator to the SAM Automatic Mask Generator, retaining the 32×32 prompt grid and 0.9 stability threshold. Other stated training and evaluation settings are unchanged. This is a reported setting revision, without evidence of rerunning experiments.

E4.justification: The token-aggregation, prompting-strategy and training-loss ablations are retained. Appendix B also preserves the attention-supervision experiment and point-prompts-versus-learnable-queries analysis, with no new robustness tests or case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The figures retain the same reporting practices.

E6.justification: Benchmark values, plotted findings and appendix ablation results are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains REN's 0.40 stAP and 0.52 tAP, Table 5 retains 0.52 mAP and 0.65 mRP@50, and Table 10 retains the same attention-supervision results.

T1.justification: The contrastive and feature-similarity equations, combined training loss, aggregation rule and Appendix B attention-supervision loss are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and scientific claims: efficient region tokens, approximately 60× faster generation and 35× lower memory, transfer to other encoders, and strong downstream performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of retrieval and segmentation performance remain unchanged, as do the limitations concerning point-prompt ambiguity and segmentation precision. Appendix B's interpretations of attention supervision and learnable queries, and Appendix C's impact discussion, are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-site link and identifies NCSA Delta/ACCESS GPU resources, while updating the named training-mask generator. Other implementation details remain unchanged. The introduction now says code and models 'will' be released, although the abstract still says they are available; actual resource withdrawal is not established.

R1.justification: Section 2's research positioning and all 55 reference entries are retained. The training description switches between already-cited SAM 2 and SAM works without changing the novelty argument or related-work coverage.

P1.justification: v2 expands Figure 1's explanatory caption, makes small release-wording edits, expands acknowledgements and replaces the preprint footer with NeurIPS 2025 information. The section sequence and almost all scientific prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 2 to page 3 and becomes a two-panel diagram explicitly illustrating both training objectives. Other displays undergo reflow, and Tables 2–3 add bold emphasis to leading baseline values without changing scores. The remaining figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded Figure 1 and caption explain the existing supervision targets more clearly and explicitly distinguish training-time segmentation from inference. Improved table emphasis also helps readers identify leading baselines. These are modest presentation gains; empirical evidence is unchanged, and the unexplained SAM 2-to-SAM revision does not establish a validated methodological improvement.
